column3: Clothing ad; "appearance of an Aurora Borealis" is only a hook for mocking newspaper prose; no sighting or place described.
Balloon night voyage: "mellow, phosphorescent atmosphere", "light enough to see our watch time" at midnight; a glowing, lit-up night sky seen.
Only sky event is an old hunter's 1833 California memory, "heavens were blazing ... with me tcors" (meteors); not an aurora.
Humorous story about a judge at a wedding; no aurora or glowing sky mentioned.
Northern Lights, in rare and unusual state of brilliancy visible Sunday night "in this latitude" from sunset until daybreak.
Aurora is the town Aurora Center, scene of a hotel burglary; no sky described.
During the auroral display eff [of] Thursday night in Boston places a visible aurora at Boston, beyond the telegraph effects.
Report on the Syracuse Democratic convention brawl; "lighting gang" is OCR for fighting; no sky phenomenon.
Weather item; cool air blamed on the "Second visit of the Aurora Borealis"; aurora cited only as a cause, no sighting described.
Hat ad asserts "the superb northern lights nearly every night" and likes hats "better than the aurora"; claims the lights are being seen.
Poem dated night of August 28, 1859 hails "Lights Of the North" that "glow", "Blazing out" with "red lightning" forms; a specific display described.
News miscellany; aurora appears only in the "FINE WRITING" clothing ad, "appearance Of an Aurora Boreals"; no sighting described.
The light seen in Borealis, was very vivid, and was an exhibition seldom witnessed in this latitude precedes general science text.
Article on the Irish religious revival and physical prostrations; no aurora or glowing sky.
News items include "The late Aurora BoieAlis was sesn in Eng land and excited much attention" (seen in England).
Frost item; "recent boreal phenomena" cited only as followed by frosts in Canada and New England; no sighting described.
Northern Lights: citizens saw "streams of lurid light ascending towards the zenith" Sunday evening, visible nearly the whole night.
Love poem about moon, stars and evening bells; no aurora or glowing sky described.
Religious sermon on Christ's wounds in heaven; no sky phenomenon described.
the whole heavens were lighted by the aurora borealis, deep red with streaks, "thousands witnessed it".
Miscellany of jokes and puns; no aurora or lit-up sky mentioned.
Family Herald contents listing; "The Aurora" is only a teaser heading, no sighting described.
General science essay on shooting stars and solar ejection; no aurora sighting.
Clothing ad opens with "The appearance of an Aurora Borealis" written up by editors "all over the country".
Last week was remarkable for Borealis and Frosts; cites "the recent displays" of the magnetic storm (Cleveland Leader).
Fiction about the runaway boy Fritz at sea; no aurora or glowing sky.
the auroral display of Thursday at Boston named alongside the telegraph operators' auroral-current exchange.
Southern Aurora Mills is a mill name damaged by storm; no sky described.
Ad says "the superb northern lights visible nearly night and day" this fall season; "hats better than the aurora".
Virginia tidewater travel letter; no aurora or glowing sky mentioned.
Washington operator: "the aurora had made its appearance", "aurora disappeared a little after ten o'clock", "During the display"; visibility reported, not only wire trouble.
Patent medicine advertisement for Judson's Mountain Herb Pills; no aurora or night sky mentioned.
Historical essay relays specific sightings: "were seen a great many bright arches"; aurora "seen and described by Mr. Bayard Taylor", Northern Europe, winter 1856-57.
Clothing ad opens with a passing mention of a sighting: "The appearance of an Aurora Borealis has afforded newspaper editors... all over the country".
Only telegraph disruption "under the influence of the Aurora Borealis" between Quebec and Farther Point; no sighting or sky described.
Havana letter: "that rare phenomenon in this latitude an aurora borealis visible in this city. It was of extraordinary beauty."
Northern Light is a steamship sailing for Aspinwall; marine news with no sky described.
Passing mention of the aurora as a current local sight: "in addition to the attraction of the aurora borealis" during this week.
Balloon night trip: "It did not become dark"; glowing vapor lit everything "as If Illuminated by torches"; a lit-up night sky, not an excluded source.
Garbled OCR of a Revolutionary War battle narrative; no aurora or glowing night sky described.
J. Wise: "there appeared in the northern heavens" a phosphorescent light, unlike ordinary aurora, so bright "it started the fire companies".
Clothing ad opens with a passing mention of a sighting: "The appearance of an Aurora Borealis has afforded newspaper editors... all over the country".
Everett oration on Webster statue in Boston; no aurora or glowing sky mentioned.
Since the appearance of the Aurora Borealis asserts the aurora appeared locally; passing mention before the dairy dispute.
Iron works advertisement; "SKY-LIGHTS" are building skylights, not a sky display.
The recurrence of the Northern lights, on the 2nd inst mentions the aurora appearing, inside a letter mostly about telegraph effects.
Keokuk local items on rain, mails, schools and railroads; no aurora or lit sky.
Telegraph report of a destructive fire at Norfolk; fire, not an aurora.
Serenade poem about bright orbs and "the midnight moon"; no aurora sighting.
Mocks Merriam's claim to own "pieces of the auroral light" like silk threads; a specimen claim, no display seen.
the northern sky has been lit up by an unusually fine aurora for some evenings past; vivid local description.
Marine list: "Northern Light" is a steamship at Sandy Hook; no sky display.
Poems; "glow of the sunset on the snow" is a sunset simile, not an aurora.
Pittsburgh Chronicle's "account of the Northern Light of Friday morning" and "the brilliant electrical display of this morning" describe a sighting.
Council Bluffs snipe-hunt story; the "light" is a lantern held by the Mayor.
Romantic fiction; "light of a full moon" on her features, no aurora.
The Aurora Borealis, seen from the summit of Mount Washington on the night of the 25th of August is a sighting.
The appearance of an Aurora Borealis prompted editors "all over the country" to describe it; passing mention in a clothing ad.
the aurora borealis tried the same game refers only to telegraph working; nothing says it was seen.
Texas account of escape from Indians; no aurora or glowing sky.
The aurora Borealis continues to be the subject of talk in Richmond; only gossip and theory, no sighting described.
Iowa political debate, newsboy honesty story and Wisconsin frost; no aurora or glowing sky mentioned.
Headline "The Aurora Borealis as Seen in Europe" reports a relayed sighting in Europe, though the body excerpt covers other news.
Poem "The Patter of Little Feet"; only "the glory of sunset", no aurora sighting.
Mock-scientific explanation of "the recent celestial visitor"'s origin; no specific sighting or place described.
Exchanges from Toronto to Louisville give "glowing descriptions of the aurora borealis" Sunday night; display "greater to the west of us than here."
On Thursday night there was another magnificent exhibition of the Aurora Borealis... The whole Northern Heavens were illumined.
Telegraph "under the influence of the aurora on Sunday night" could not be worked; telegraph effects only, no sighting described.
